text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A senior police officer and a constable are among 18 people killed during an exchange of fire in Marsabit district near the border with Ethiopia.
- An earth tremor shakes Nairobi and its environs.
- Kenya Posts & Telecommunications reduces charges for regional calls by 62 percent beginning April 1.
- Unionisable bank employees in the country threaten to go on strike following the collapse of talks with the Kenya Bankers Employers Association over their medical scheme.
- Amani Counselling Centre in Nairobi says it is time Kenyans stopped denying existence of homosexuality in schools.
- The fire brigade in Nairobi and Machakos ignore desperate pleas from fire victims in Athi River on Nairobi's outskirts.
- A Nairobi chief magistrate refuses to soften bail terms for opposition parliamentarian Njehu Gatabaki, charged with sedition.
- The inquest into the mysterious death of University of Nairobi student leader Solomon Muruli begins on April 7.
- Police are investigating a series of financial scandals that have so far fleeced Kenyatta University more than 100 million shillings ($1.82 million)
- Foreign Affairs Minister Kalonzo Musyoka is marshalling the support of power-maker Nicholas Biwott to boost his image. ($1=55 Kenyan Shillings)
